recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-51566's Observation.referenceRange.low/high scope; future datatype-level exclusive-bound work should use separate Jira decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-51566 was Applied with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It requested changing Observation.referenceRange.low and .high from SimpleQuantity to Quantity, constraining low.comparator to >= or > and high.comparator to <= or <, preserving inclusive absent-comparator defaults, and adding explanatory text.
initial_application: No prior AutoFHIR reconcile commit existed. Upstream commits fa4bcdc63c0bbd2f43471b7df164a1363c16d5fb and ee556b3d7cdb7e22b4c434f48544f5f65924b0e6 applied the FHIR-51566 changes in October 2025 through HL7/fhir pull requests #3707 and #3723.
additional_context: FHIR-8551 established the historical inclusive default and rejected an extension. FHIR-5165 is background for the Quantity/SimpleQuantity comparator distinction. Zulip and OO minutes show broader Range/Age questions, including FHIR-22642 and FHIR-45021, were considered but remained outside FHIR-51566's Observation-only applied scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Observation StructureDefinition has Quantity on low/high, obs-13 and obs-14 comparator constraints, comments explaining inclusive defaults and explicit comparator meanings, plus examples and invariant tests for allowed/disallowed comparator directions.

related_jiras.note: Established the inclusive default for Observation.referenceRange.low/high when no comparator is present.

Related Range/Age clarity issue cited in Zulip and minutes but not decided by this Observation-specific audit.
